c.tagline: Diamond capital of Rubens, fashion, and Flemish grandeur.

taxi.fareNote: Licensed taxis run on the meter with a rooftop sign; they are usually booked by app or taken from ranks at Central Station and squares rather than hailed on the street.

emergency.note: 112 is the general EU emergency number for ambulance and fire; 101 reaches the police directly.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.Het Eilandje: MAS Museum aan de Stroom Antwerp

avoid.reason: Watch for pickpockets around Central Station and De Coninckplein, which get seedy late at night.

hood_desc: The medieval core around the Grote Markt guild houses, the Cathedral of Our Lady, and the Rubenshuis; best for first-timers who want the landmarks, cobbled streets, and cafes all within a short walk.
The stylish southern district of grand avenues, the KMSKA and FoMu museums, galleries, and a dense strip of bars and restaurants; suits travellers after dining and nightlife with an arty edge.
The revitalised old-docklands quarter on the river, anchored by the striking MAS museum, marinas, warehouse lofts, and waterfront eateries; good for a trendy, up-and-coming base.
The fashion quarter around Nationalestraat and the MoMu fashion museum, lined with the boutiques of the 'Antwerp Six' and independent designers; a paradise for shoppers and style-seekers.
The bustling area around the cathedral-like Antwerpen-Centraal station, taking in the diamond district and a compact Chinatown; a convenient, well-connected base for arriving by train.
lodging: Radisson Blu Hotel, Antwerp City Centre

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink throughout the city.

transit.pay: De Lijn tickets are cheapest bought before boarding via the app, machines, or shops (about €2.50 a ride); contactless bank cards also work when tapping on board. A day pass is around €7.50. Several central tram lines run underground as a 'premetro'.
transit.hours: Trams and buses run roughly 5:30am to midnight; night service is limited to a few weekend lines, with taxis and ride apps filling the late gap.
transit.note: Antwerp has no full metro, but its tram network dives underground as a 'premetro' through the city centre.

transit.m: Train from Brussels Airport (BRU) to Antwerpen-Centraal, ~35-45 min

tip.r: Service is included in the bill; rounding up or leaving 5-10% for good service is appreciated but not expected.

landmarks: Cathedral of Our Lady (Onze-Lieve-Vrouwekathedraal)
Belgium's largest Gothic cathedral soars over the city center with its lacy spire and houses masterpieces by Rubens. Its interior is a breathtaking blend of art and architecture.
Grote Markt
This picture-perfect market square is ringed by gilded guild houses and the ornate Renaissance city hall. It's the lively, photogenic heart of Antwerp's old town.
Antwerp Central Station
Often called the 'Railway Cathedral,' this monumental station dazzles with its soaring domed hall, marble, and gold detailing. Even non-travelers stop by just to admire the architecture.
Het Steen
This medieval fortress on the Scheldt riverbank is Antwerp's oldest building and once guarded the city's harbor. Its stout stone towers make a striking waterfront photo.
MAS (Museum aan de Stroom)
This striking spiral-shaped museum tower offers a free rooftop panorama over the city and port. Its bold red-stone and glass design is a symbol of Antwerp's modern renewal.
Rubens House (Rubenshuis)

Step into the opulent home and studio of Baroque master Peter Paul Rubens, filled with his paintings and personal artifacts. The elegant garden and courtyard transport you back to 17th-century splendor.
Antwerp Diamond District
As the world's diamond capital, this glittering district is packed with cutters, traders, and sparkling shop windows. It's a fascinating (and dazzling) walk even if you're not buying.
Antwerp Zoo
One of the oldest zoos in the world sits right next to Central Station behind a striking Egyptian-style facade. It's a beloved family attraction wrapped in beautiful historic architecture.
Vlaeykensgang
This tiny hidden medieval alley tucked behind the cathedral feels like a secret pocket of old Antwerp. Wandering its cobblestones at dusk is a magical, lantern-lit experience.
Scheldt River Promenade
Stroll along the riverfront for sweeping views of Het Steen, passing ships, and the modern MAS skyline. It's a favorite spot for both sunset photos and a relaxed evening walk.

train.note: Antwerpen-Centraal is one of Europe's most beautiful stations and sits on the high-speed line north, so the Amsterdam and Rotterdam services stop here directly - Amsterdam is about an hour away. Eurostar trains to London and Paris also call. Brussels is 45 minutes by domestic train. Book international services on the operator sites; Belgian domestic fares are fixed-price with no advance discount.

bus.note: Coaches use the Antwerpen-Berchem station stop rather than Centraal - one stop south on the local train. FlixBus dominates, with Amsterdam about 2 hours away and Paris 4. Carry your passport for London services, which include a full UK immigration check at the Channel.

ferry.note: Antwerp is Europe's second-largest port but handles containers, not scheduled passengers. Small free ferries cross the Scheldt to the Left Bank in the city, and the Sint-Anna pedestrian tunnel does the same on foot. International sailings leave from Zeebrugge, about 90 minutes west, with P&O to Hull.
